summary: During the ASEAN-EU Ministerial Meeting in Brunei, Thailand informed Cambodia of its intent to withdraw from the 2001 MOU regarding overlapping maritime claims. Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow argued the 20-year-old pact failed to produce progress and stated Thailand would prefer to use UNCLOS principles for future negotiations.
title: This Week in Peace: Thailand to Terminate MOU for Maritime Cooperation with Cambodia

summary: The Thai government is preparing to revoke a 25-year-old maritime Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Cambodia. Officials stated the move aims to shift toward using international law, specifically UNCLOS, to break the long-standing deadlock over energy-rich overlapping claims in the Gulf of Thailand.
title: Thailand eyes UN maritime law to resolve Cambodia border dispute

summary: Thai authorities repatriated 55 Cambodian migrant workers (34 men, 19 women, and 2 boys) through the Khlong Luek border checkpoint in Sa Kaeo. The handover occurred at the Thai-Cambodian Friendship Bridge under the supervision of the Burapha Task Force after the workers' legal cases in Thailand were concluded.
title: Thailand repatriates 55 Cambodian workers via border

summary: Analysts and experts have dismissed claims made by Thailand's UN Ambassador Cherdchai Chaivaivid, who argued that Thailand's historical support for Cambodia's development should mitigate criticism of its current military actions. Critics argue that past humanitarian aid does not excuse alleged violations of sovereignty or 'indiscriminate armed attacks.' The report notes that thousands of Cambodian households remain displaced near the border due to blockades and explosive remnants from the 2025 conflict.
title: Experts reject Thai claims of past aid to justify actions against Cambodia

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow announced that Thailand is awaiting a response from Cambodia regarding a proposed trilateral meeting including the Philippines. The talks are intended to take place on the sidelines of the 48th ASEAN Summit in the Philippines from May 7 to 9, 2026. The meeting aims to address regional stability and the ongoing bilateral tensions.
title: Thai Foreign Minister expects Cambodia to join trilateral talks at ASEAN summit

summary: Acting Head of State Hun Sen warned that Thailand's push to cancel the 2001 maritime agreement risks dismantling a long-standing framework for managing overlapping claims in the Gulf of Thailand. He suggested the move might be driven by internal nationalism and questioned if Thailand is attempting to internationalize the dispute rather than sticking to bilateral talks.
title: Hun Sen warns Thai move to end maritime MoU may fuel row

summary: The Thai Cabinet approved the cancellation of the 2001 maritime agreement with Cambodia to align future negotiations with UNCLOS. Thai officials cited the need to update the framework after two decades without tangible results. Thailand plans to establish technical and legal committees to manage the new framework while maintaining that it remains committed to international law.
title: Thailand scraps maritime agreement with Cambodia, turns to UN framework

summary: Cambodia announced it will initiate a compulsory conciliation mechanism under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) after the Thai Cabinet canceled the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44). Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn expressed regret, stating the MOU was the 'only bilateral framework' for addressing overlapping claims. Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul stated the cancellation was due to stalled progress and would not harm relations.
title: Cambodia to seek UN intervention over maritime claims after Thailand withdraws from agreement

summary: The Thai cabinet unilaterally terminated the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) with Cambodia regarding overlapping maritime claims in the Gulf of Thailand. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated the cancellation was due to a lack of progress over 25 years and was an election promise. Cambodia's Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn expressed regret and announced that Phnom Penh will now pursue compulsory conciliation under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). The decision follows two rounds of armed conflict last year that killed close to 150 people.
title: Thailand scraps 25-year-old agreement with Cambodia on joint energy exploration

summary: Cambodian Secretary of State Kung Phoak stated that Cambodia is prepared to invoke international legal mechanisms under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) if Thailand unilaterally withdraws from the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). This move signals a shift from bilateral talks to international mediation. Thailand's Cabinet is reportedly expected to meet today to consider the proposal to withdraw from the MoU, which has governed overlapping claims in the Gulf of Thailand for 25 years.
title: Cambodia signals UNCLOS route if Thailand scraps maritime MoU

summary: Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn stated that Cambodia will initiate the compulsory conciliation mechanism under UNCLOS after Thailand's withdrawal from the 2001 MOU. He described the move as a departure from the spirit of peaceful resolution while clarifying that the termination does not affect Cambodia's lawful rights over its maritime areas.
title: Cambodia to initiate compulsory conciliation mechanism under UNCLOS after Thailand scraps maritime dispute pact: FM

summary: The Thai Cabinet officially approved the termination of the 2001 MOU on overlapping maritime claims on May 5, 2026. Government officials stated that Thailand will now transition to using UNCLOS as the primary legal framework for future negotiations. The government is currently establishing a new technical and legal committee to handle the maritime boundary issues moving forward, insisting that the move is an adjustment of the 'cooperation framework' rather than an end to diplomatic dialogue.
title: Cabinet Approves Termination of the 2001 MOU between Thailand and Cambodia

summary: Thailand has ended a 2001 agreement meant to resolve overlapping maritime claims with Cambodia. While the deal aimed to peacefully manage marine resources and oil/gas exploitation, five rounds of talks over two decades yielded no results. The termination comes amid strained relations following border clashes in July and December 2025, which displaced hundreds of thousands. Cambodia stated it would continue to seek a resolution despite the Thai cabinet's move.
title: Thailand scraps 2001 maritime territory deal with Cambodia after years of deadlock

summary: Reporting on the Thai Cabinet's decision to scrap the 2001 maritime pact, this source highlights that Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn expressed regret over the move. Cambodia now plans to pursue 'compulsory conciliation' under UNCLOS, a process where an independent commission hears both sides to propose solutions. The report notes that while a ceasefire has been in place since December, the underlying border and maritime disputes remain unresolved after heavy fighting in 2025.
title: Thailand scraps Cambodia pact on energy exploration

summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. mediated a historic handshake between Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul and Cambodian PM Hun Manet on May 7, 2026, in Cebu. The leaders agreed to extend the mandate of the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) until July and directed their ministries to avoid further escalation after a conflict that killed nearly 150 people since mid-2025.
title: Marcos plays peacemaker for Thailand, Cambodia at ASEAN 2026

summary: Leaders from Thailand and Cambodia met in Cebu, Philippines, for rare talks following deadly border fighting in July and December of last year. While a ceasefire is currently holding, troops remain deployed along the 817-km border. The meeting, facilitated by the Philippines as ASEAN Chair, aimed to create a stable atmosphere for the regional summit. Tensions recently spiked after Thailand unilaterally ended a 25-year-old maritime energy exploration pact.
title: Thai, Cambodian leaders to meet on ASEAN sidelines amid uneasy truce

summary: Trilateral talks involving Philippines President Marcos, Cambodian PM Hun Manet, and Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul led to agreements on de-escalation and maintaining open communication. The leaders agreed to extend the mandate of the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) for another three months to monitor the border ceasefire. While specific border demarcations were not discussed, both sides tasked their foreign ministers to continue operational-level dialogues.
title: Cambodia, Thailand Make Progress In Border Talks At ASEAN Summit

summary: Following a trilateral meeting in Cebu, Thailand and Cambodia have pledged to restore diplomatic ties that were downgraded after deadly border clashes in 2025. Foreign ministers from both nations will implement 'confidence-building measures' immediately, focusing on shared interests to maintain the current uneasy truce.
title: 'Let's live in peace,' Thailand and Cambodia pledge to rebuild ties after deadly clashes

summary: The Cambodian National Assembly has approved extending military conscription to two years and increasing penalties for draft evasion. This legislative development follows ongoing border clashes and heightened tensions with Thailand.
title: Cambodian National Assembly extends military conscription amid Thailand border tensions

summary: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet stated during a parliamentary session that Cambodia will reject new bilateral negotiations with Thailand regarding their maritime dispute. Instead, the country will pursue a compulsory conciliation mechanism under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). This position follows Thailand's unilateral termination of the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU 2001) concerning overlapping maritime claims on May 5. Hun Manet argued that it is unreasonable for Thailand to cancel the bilateral framework and then expect new bilateral talks, stating that if Thailand wanted to negotiate bilaterally, it should have kept the MoU 2001.
title: Cambodia to pursue UN legal mechanism, rejecting bilateral talks with Thailand over maritime dispute: PM

summary: A Thai Senate committee has recommended the revocation of the 2000 MoU 43, arguing it is legally flawed and overly reliant on disputed French-era maps. The committee suggests that recent ceasefire agreements and new border control mechanisms should serve as the new reference point for future relations, as the current framework has failed to prevent tensions.
title: Senate panel urges scrapping of MOU43, citing legal flaws and disputed maps

summary: Thai rangers from the 12th Ranger Control Unit and Khok Sung Task Force deployed to inspect a disputed border section near Ang Sila village, Non Mak Mun subdistrict, Khok Sung district, Sa Kaeo province. This followed reports that Cambodian villagers brought tractors to plow land for farming in an area Thai authorities claim crossed outside the designated boundary line. Thai rangers held discussions with Cambodian military personnel on the ground. Both sides reached an initial agreement for the Cambodian villagers to halt all land preparation activities until the territorial boundary line in the area is officially surveyed and clarified by border demarcation officials.
title: Thai rangers halt Cambodian farming activity in Sa Kaeo border area

summary: Following Thailand's revocation of the MoU 44 maritime agreement on May 5, Cambodia plans to pursue compulsory conciliation under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). Experts suggest this is a strategic move to address overlapping maritime claims, though it remains unclear if this will lead to full delimitation or joint development.
title: Experts back Cambodia's UNCLOS conciliation plan for overlapping maritime claims with Thailand

summary: Cambodia is urging Thailand to resume border talks and joint demarcation work. Thailand has requested a delay to these meetings while it reshuffles its negotiation team following recent cabinet changes. Cambodia maintains that boundary work must follow the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) framework and established historical maps, rejecting any unilateral changes to the border.
title: Thailand reshuffles JBC team amid renewed call for talks

summary: Following a trilateral meeting in Cebu on May 7, 2026, Thailand and Cambodia agreed to rebuild trust and ease tensions along their border. Facilitated by Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., the leaders committed to sustaining dialogue and preventing actions that could lead to further escalation.
title: Cebu peace trilaterals signal PH, ASEAN push for peace, dialogue

summary: The Commander-in-Chief of the Royal Thai Army met with the head of the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) from the Philippines to reaffirm a joint commitment to maintaining stability along the Thai-Cambodian border. The mission aims to ensure neutrality and oversight following high-level trilateral meetings to de-escalate tensions.
title: Army Chief Welcomes AOT, Affirming Border Stability

summary: A Thai Senate committee briefed diplomats from ASEAN+3 on Thailand's decision to revoke the 2000 and 2001 Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) with Cambodia, arguing the agreements failed to resolve disputes and undermined national interests.
title: Thai Panel Defends Scrapping Border MOUs to ASEAN+3 Diplomats

title: Thai PM Anutin reaffirms Thai-Cambodian border crossings remain closed

summary: Cambodia has welcomed Thailand's proposal to resume bilateral border talks, including meetings between defense ministers and committees like the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC), to reduce tensions and strengthen mutual trust.
title: Cambodia welcomes Thai return to negotiating table amid push for stability

title: Anutin says ‘no reopening’ of border with Cambodia despite economic strain

title: Thailand urges Cambodia to face facts on scam centres after Hun Sen remarks

title: National Assembly welcomes EU parliament call for peaceful border resolution

He urged Cambodia to stop making accusations to allow for constructive progress on bilateral issues.
title: Thailand never claimed others' land, DPM Sihasak tells United Nations Security Council

title: Cambodia ready to advance Thailand border pact

title: Thai PM's map rejection sparks new tensions with Cambodia

title: Cambodia protests Thai construction activities in occupied border areas

title: Cambodia exposes Thai military expansion in disputed territory
